name: A task was assigned to you
description: Hands someone a piece of work: what it is, who gave it to them, when it is due and how urgent it is, in that order.

origin.note: Design: work item — a priority bar above everything, the due date alone in its own tinted band, one full-width action, and the tracker facts held back until after it.

subject: Assigned to you: {{ task_title }}
preheader: The due date and the priority are both above the fold; the tracker detail sits under the button.

task_title.description: The work itself, in the words the tracker holds. It carries the subject line too, so a title written as "fix it" produces an unusable email.
task_title.example: Rewrite the CSV importer's retry logic

project_name.description: Which board, project or client this belongs to. Set as the eyebrow, because someone holding six projects needs it before they read the title.

assigned_by.description: Who handed the work over. Work arrives from a person, not from a system, and naming them is what makes the task negotiable.

assigned_at.description: When the assignment happened, for the record kept under the button.

task_reference.description: The tracker's own identifier, shown monospaced so it can be pasted into a branch name or a standup without transcription errors.

task_description.description: A short brief on what finished looks like. Deliberately placed under the action rather than above it, so the reader can open the task without reading it.
task_description.example: The current backoff is exponential in name only and retries three times in under a second. Move it to a real backoff with jitter and cap total retry time at two minutes.

priority_level.description: Severity of the priority bar. Carried as a word, a shape and a rule weight as well as a colour, so it survives a client that inverts the palette.

priority_label.description: The urgency in one word. Use the vocabulary your team already argues in, not the tracker's internal enum.

priority_text.description: Why it carries that priority. "High" on its own is a colour; "High — blocking the September release" is a reason someone can act on or push back against.

due_label.description: Heading over the date band. Change it when your team says "target" or "needed by" rather than "due".

due_at.description: The date, set as the largest thing in the message after the title. Written out rather than numeric, because 09/11 means two different days on two continents.

due_relative.description: The same date as a distance — "in four working days". People act on the distance and forget the date.

no_due_text.description: What the band says when there is no date. An empty band would read as a rendering fault, and "no date" is itself information worth stating.
no_due_text.default: No date set. Ask whoever assigned it before you plan around it.

estimate.description: How much work this was sized at, if your team sizes work. It is the fact people use to decide whether to accept the assignment today or tomorrow.

action_label.description: Label on the full-width action. Name the task, not the tool.

action_url.description: Deep link to the task itself, so accepting or reassigning it is one tap rather than a search through a board.

notification_settings_url.description: Where assignment mail gets batched or turned off. Someone on a busy board may want a daily list instead of twelve of these.

notification_settings_label.description: Wording of that link. Offer the frequency, not the preferences page.
notification_settings_label.default: Change how often you get these
